answer: Anchor admission to a proof-of-burn bridged from a public external chain: to mint one identity you must irreversibly destroy real value there and present that transaction as a bridge receipt, timestamped by a shared randomness beacon so it cannot be back-dated or reused. Peers audit each receipt against the beacon's reef of already-claimed burns and reject duplicates. A sybil fleet cannot share one burn: every mask needs its own destroyed stake, so N fakes cost N irreversible burns, not a one-time mint.
